children: has a cloud-sized test ahead: turn rapid growth into earnings and cash. Shares rose 0.38% to $523.88 at 9:40 a.m. ET on November 2. Baird raised its price target to $600 from $500 on October 30 while maintaining Outperform, citing acceleration in Azure and Microsoft 365. With Microsoft Cloud generating nearly seven dollars of every ten in quarterly revenue, execution carries substantial weight.

Microsoft's October 28 release put quarterly revenue at $92.279 billion, including $63.9 billion from Microsoft Clouda calculated 69.2% of the total. Azure grew 48%, while commercial remaining performance obligations climbed 73% to $677 billion. That backlog points to substantial contracted demand, but it has yet to become recognized revenue. Delivering enough capacity to serve customers could determine how quickly those commitments translate into results.

The GuruFocus snapshot shows a perfect GF Score of 100/100 and a price-to-earnings ratio of 27.36, with strong readings across profitability, growth and valuation. Financial strength scores comparatively lower on the radar, and the screen flags one severe warning without identifying it. The picture supports a strong overall assessment while leaving a specific risk unresolved. For investors, the next test extends beyond Azure's growth rate: cloud margins and cash conversion will help show whether expansion is producing durable financial returns.

title: Microsoft Stocks Move Higher With Cloud Growth Supporting Baird's Higher Target
